newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coal mine resumes shipments to port.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coal mine resumes shipments to port.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 14 Reuter - Repair work on the railway linking Colombia's sprawling Cerrejon Norte coal mine with the Caribbean coast were completed over the weekend and shipments have resumed, the mine's operators said.
They said the first shipments from the mine to port since the railway was severely damaged in an attack by suspected leftist guerrillas on April 8 were made on Sunday.
The mine, operated by Exxon subsidiary Intercor and state-run Carbones de Colombia, is the largest open-pit coal mine in Latin America.

More than 1,640 feet of track were damaged in the dynamite attack, which caused the derailing of 27 railway cars filled with 2,700 metric tons of coal and the spillage of 3,700 gallons 14,000 litres of diesel fuel.
Colombia is the world's fourth largest producer of coal after Australia, Poland and South Africa.
